1) the protein profiles of cancer cell populations, whether histologically indeterminate or identified, recapitulate phylogenetic ontogeny; and 2) the protein profiles, when compared to one another, can be used to identify cancer cell populations of different embryologic stem cell origin.

the qualitative content of cellular proteins is characteristic of stem cells of origin of the cancer cell.

the development of an analytical method to identify human cancers by comparing the qualitative protein content of cancer cells with that of normal cells from which they are derived.
the identification of human cancers of unknown histologic type.
the identification of histologic indeterminate human cancers using two-dimensional protein electrophoretic analysis of stained proteins.

the qualitative distribution of proteins in human cancer cells, as revealed by two-dimensional electroporesis and scanning densitometry, is a reflection of the stem cell origin of the cancer.
